finding.claim: Broken authorization: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws. The result is discarded, so any caller can wipe any tenant. The sibling export() uses checkRole(), which throws, and is enforced correctly.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (with no OWNER role) calling POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, with an attacker-chosen tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive tenant data wipe.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called and its boolean return value is ignored.
requireRole just returns u.roles().contains(role); the javadoc at line 13 says it does not throw, so a missing role has no effect.

finding.guards_checked: The only control on the path is requireRole at line 26, and its result is unused, so it is not enforced. Compared with export() at line 32, which uses checkRole and throws SecurityException at line 20. No other auth check, tenant ownership check or middleware exists in the repo, which has one file.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:26 (returns boolean, never throws, result discarded) — ineffective; checkRole (line 18) throws but is only used in export() at line 32. No other controls; src/Admin.java is the only file.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, a boolean-returning function (lines 14-15, javadoc line 13 says it does not throw) whose result is discarded, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike export() which correctly uses the throwing checkRole at line 32.
